KLEIMAN'S PROOF OF CLAUSE (1) RUNS THROUGH th:repDiv (HILBERT SCHEME) AND lm:qt -- so the seam's ORIGINAL docstring was right about its inputs, and the 2026-07-29 'ROUTE QUESTION, RESOLVED' overstates. AJC has TWO routes to one obligation and the board describes one.

th:main L2155-L2166 verbatim: 'Assume f: X -> S is projective Zariski locally over S, and is flat with integral geometric fibers. (1) Then Pic_{X/S} exists, is separated and locally of finite type over S, and represents Pic_{(X/S)et}.'

THAT IS CLAUSE (1), EXACTLY -- representable, separated, locally of finite type, NO rational-point hypothesis. Clause (1) is a THEOREM IN THE LITERATURE for a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over any field. Only its formalisation is open.

ITS PROOF (inside th:main, which reduces (1) to (2)): 'Consider the Abel map A_{X/S}: Div_{X/S} -> P. Note that Div_{X/S} is a scheme, in fact, an open subscheme of the Hilbert scheme Hilb_{X/S}, by Theorem th:repDiv.' Then it descends by lm:qt.

th:repDiv L1837: 'Assume X/S is projective and flat. Then Div_{X/S} is representable by an open subscheme of the Hilbert scheme Hilb_{X/S}.'

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE BOARD. AJC.picrep says the docstring's prescription of th:repDiv + the Altman-Kleiman quotient lemma is 'simply wrong' because both belong to the REJECTED route. As a claim about which route AJC CHOSE, true. As published -- a claim about what discharging the sorry NEEDS -- false: the docstring was naming the inputs of the only published proof of its own statement. Note th:repDiv is HILBERT, not Quot, so 'the route needs Quot' was imprecise in the original too, and rejecting AJC.picrep.quot does not reject th:repDiv.

PLANNING CONSEQUENCE: the ten absent Milne-Kollar modules are ONE route. Kleiman's own proof is a SECOND -- and it is the one whose lm:qt interface AJC already has pinned (HasSmoothProperQuotient/smoothProperQuotient, currently labelled P -> P, zero instances) while building its Div side through the GRASSMANNIAN (D2'-D4') instead of Hilb. 15	# Galois descent for semilinear representations (Speiser's theorem)
16	
17	This file supplies the **finite Galois descent** substrate for the FGA Picard-scheme
18	representability campaign (`instHasPicScheme`, cluster `G` of
19	`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`): milestone `G2(b)` (Speiser's
20	semilinear descent) and its consumers `G1`/`G3`.
21	
22	Let `L/K` be a finite Galois extension with group `G = Gal(L/K) = L ≃ₐ[K] L`, and
23	let `V` be an `L`-vector space equipped with a **semilinear** `G`-action, i.e. an
24	additive `G`-action with
25	`σ • (a • v) = σ a • (σ • v)` for `σ ∈ G`, `a ∈ L`, `v ∈ V` (`IsSemilinear`).
26	The `K`-subspace of invariants `V^G` (`SemilinearAction.invariants`) is a `K`-form
27	of `V`: the canonical `L`-linear map
28	
29	`descentMap : L ⊗[K] V^G → V`,  `a ⊗ v ↦ a • v`
30	
31	is an **isomorphism** (`descentEquiv`), so `dim_K V^G = dim_L V`. This is Speiser's
32	theorem — Galois descent for vector spaces — the algebraic heart of the finite
33	Galois quotient engine `G2`.
34	
35	## Main definitions and results
36	
37	* `IsSemilinear K L V` — the semilinearity hypothesis on a `G`-action.
38	* `SemilinearAction.invariants K L V : Submodule K V` — the fixed subspace `V^G`.
39	* `SemilinearAction.avg K L a v : V` — the averaging element `∑_σ σ a • (σ • v)`,
40	  which always lies in `V^G` (`avg_mem_invariants`).
41	* `SemilinearAction.descentMap K L V : L ⊗[K] V^G →ₗ[L] V` — the descent map.
42	* `SemilinearAction.descentMap_bijective` / `descentEquiv` — Speiser's theorem.
43	
44	## Mathlib inputs

47	(`linearIndependent_algHom_toLinearMap`): the `K`-algebra homomorphisms `L →ₐ[K] L`
48	are `L`-linearly independent as `K`-linear maps.  Combined with the finite-field
49	count `AlgHom.card`, the "Galois matrix" `(σ (b i))_{σ, i}` of a `K`-basis `b` of
50	`L` is invertible over `L`, which powers both directions of the descent isomorphism.
51

53	(Kleiman §4 uses finite Galois descent to build `Pic_{C/k}` from `Pic_{C_{k'}/k'}`;

/-- **Corollary (Galois descent of dimension).** `dim_K V^G = dim_L V`: the

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GaloisDescent.SemilinearModules

/-!
# The Galois splitting of the self-tensor `L ⊗[K] L ≃ Gal(L/K) → L`

For a **finite Galois** extension `L/K` with group `G = Gal(L/K) = L ≃ₐ[K] L`, the
`L`-algebra map

`a ⊗ b ↦ (γ ↦ a * γ b) : L ⊗[K] L → (G → L)`

is an isomorphism (`galoisSelfTensorEquiv`).  Geometrically this is the statement
that `Spec L ×_{Spec K} Spec L` is `G` copies of `Spec L` — the fact that makes
the two pullback legs of a one-element Galois cover computable, and hence the
algebra input of the *invariance* half of Galois descent for the étale-sheafified
relative Picard functor.

## Why this file exists

`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` builds the covering sieve generated by the single
morphism `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`, and `Picard/PicEtDescentAssembly.lean` proves that a
*compatible family* on that cover has a unique amalgamation.  What stands between
a `Gal(k'/k)`-**invariant** `k'`-class and such a compatible family is agreement
on the two pullback legs of the sieve, and those legs live over
`Spec (k' ⊗[k] k')`.  Identifying that ring with `Gal(k'/k) → k'` is what turns
the group-theoretic hypothesis (invariance under each `γ`) into the sheaf-theoretic
one (agreement of two restrictions).

Measured absent before being built (`ajc-p1`, run 0083 r6, and independently by
`ajc-p2` in inbox `I-1367`): `exact?` fails on `Function.Bijective` of exactly
this map, and no name-shaped search over Mathlib or either project returns it.
Mathlib's two nearest relatives are genuinely different statements:

* `Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod` — an étale algebra is *some* finite
  product of finite separable extensions, with no identification of the index set
  with `Gal(L/K)` and no formula for the map;
* `Algebra.FormallyEtale.equivPiOfIsSepClosed` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Field.lean`)
  — splits an étale algebra over a **separably closed** base, which is not the
  hypothesis here (if `K` were separably closed, `L = K`).

## Main results

* `galoisSelfTensorHom` — the `L`-algebra homomorphism `a ⊗ b ↦ (γ ↦ a * γ b)`.
* `galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective` — it is bijective.
* `galoisSelfTensorEquiv` — the resulting `L`-algebra equivalence, with
  `galoisSelfTensorEquiv_tmul` and `galoisSelfTensorEquiv_apply_tmul` for computing.

## Proof

Surjectivity is Dedekind independence in the *column* form already in this
directory: `galoisCol_span` (`GaloisDescent/SemilinearModules.lean`) says the
vectors `(γ ↦ γ (b i))` span `G → L` over `L` for a `K`-basis `b` of `L`, and
those vectors are exactly the images `galoisSelfTensorHom (1 ⊗ₜ b i)`.  Injectivity
is then a dimension count: both sides have `L`-dimension `[L : K]`
(`Module.finrank_baseChange` on the left, `#G = [L:K]` on the right by
`IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`), so a surjective `L`-linear map between them is
injective.

No hypothesis beyond `[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]`, and in particular
nothing about `K` being perfect or separably closed.
-/

universe u v

open scoped TensorProduct
open Module

namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]

/-! ## §1. The map -/

/-- The `K`-algebra map `L →ₐ[K] (Gal(L/K) → L)` sending `b` to `γ ↦ γ b`.

This is the "second leg" of the splitting: the copy of `L` that the Galois group
acts on.  It is a `K`-algebra map and not an `L`-algebra map, which is exactly why
the target is a product over `G` rather than a single copy of `L`. -/
def galoisEvalHom : L →ₐ[K] ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) where
  toFun b := fun γ => γ b
  map_one' := by ext γ; simp
  map_mul' x y := by ext γ; simp
  map_zero' := by ext γ; simp
  map_add' x y := by ext γ; simp
  commutes' r := by ext γ; simp

@[simp] lemma galoisEvalHom_apply (b : L) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    galoisEvalHom K L b γ = γ b := rfl

/-- **The Galois splitting map** `L ⊗[K] L →ₐ[L] (Gal(L/K) → L)`,
`a ⊗ b ↦ (γ ↦ a * γ b)`.

The `L`-algebra structure on the source is the one on the **left** tensor factor,
and on the target it is the diagonal (constant functions); the left factor is
carried across untwisted, the right factor by evaluation at each `γ`. -/
noncomputable def galoisSelfTensorHom : L ⊗[K] L →ₐ[L] ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (Algebra.ofId L _) (galoisEvalHom K L)
    fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _

@[simp] lemma galoisSelfTensorHom_tmul (a b : L) :
    galoisSelfTensorHom K L (a ⊗ₜ[K] b) = fun γ => a * γ b := by
  ext γ
  simp [galoisSelfTensorHom, Algebra.ofId_apply, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one]

lemma galoisSelfTensorHom_tmul_apply (a b : L) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    galoisSelfTensorHom K L (a ⊗ₜ[K] b) γ = a * γ b := by
  rw [galoisSelfTensorHom_tmul]

/-! ## §2. Bijectivity -/

section Galois

variable [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]

/-- The `L`-dimension of the target `Gal(L/K) → L` is `[L : K]`.

`#Gal(L/K) = [L:K]` is `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`; this is the only place the
Galois hypothesis (as opposed to mere finite separability) enters the dimension
count, and it is what makes the index set of the splitting the Galois group rather
than an unnamed finite set. -/
theorem finrank_pi_aut : finrank L ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) = finrank K L := by
  haveI : Fintype (L ≃ₐ[K] L) := AlgEquiv.fintype K L
  rw [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, ← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card,
    IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank K L]

/-- The splitting map is **surjective**: Dedekind independence, column form.

`galoisCol_span` says the vectors `(γ ↦ γ (b i))` span `Gal(L/K) → L` over `L`;
those vectors are the images of `1 ⊗ₜ b i`, so the range — an `L`-submodule
containing them — is everything. -/
theorem galoisSelfTensorHom_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (galoisSelfTensorHom K L) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι, b⟩ : Σ ι : Type u, Basis ι K L := ⟨_, Module.finBasis K L⟩
  haveI : Finite ι := FiniteDimensional.finite_basis b
  -- the range of the `L`-linear map underlying `galoisSelfTensorHom`
  set S : Submodule L ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) :=
    LinearMap.range (galoisSelfTensorHom K L).toLinearMap with hS
  have hspan : Submodule.span L
      (Set.range (fun i : ι => (fun γ => γ (b i) : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L))) = ⊤ :=
    galoisCol_span b
  have hsub : Submodule.span L
      (Set.range (fun i : ι => (fun γ => γ (b i) : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L))) ≤ S := by
    rw [Submodule.span_le]
    rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨(1 : L) ⊗ₜ[K] b i, by ext γ; simp⟩
  have htop : S = ⊤ := top_le_iff.mp (hspan ▸ hsub)
  intro y
  have : y ∈ S := htop ▸ Submodule.mem_top
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
  exact ⟨x, hx⟩

/-- The splitting map is **bijective**.

Injectivity is not proved directly: it follows from surjectivity because the two
`L`-modules have the same finite dimension `[L : K]` — `Module.finrank_baseChange`
on the source, `finrank_pi_aut` on the target. -/
theorem galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (galoisSelfTensorHom K L) := by
  haveI : Fintype (L ≃ₐ[K] L) := AlgEquiv.fintype K L
  have hdim : finrank L (L ⊗[K] L) = finrank L ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) := by
    rw [Module.finrank_baseChange, finrank_pi_aut]
  refine ⟨?_, galoisSelfTensorHom_surjective K L⟩
  have hfin : Module.Finite L (L ⊗[K] L) := Module.Finite.base_change L K L
  exact (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank hdim).mpr
    (galoisSelfTensorHom_surjective K L)

/-- **The Galois splitting of the self-tensor.** For a finite Galois extension
`L/K`, the `L`-algebra map `a ⊗ b ↦ (γ ↦ a * γ b)` is an isomorphism

`L ⊗[K] L ≃ₐ[L] (Gal(L/K) → L)`.

Scheme-theoretically: `Spec L ×_{Spec K} Spec L ≅ ⨿_{γ ∈ Gal(L/K)} Spec L`. This
is the computation of the two pullback legs of a one-element Galois cover, i.e.
the algebra input of the invariance half of Galois descent. -/
noncomputable def galoisSelfTensorEquiv : (L ⊗[K] L) ≃ₐ[L] ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) :=
  AlgEquiv.ofBijective (galoisSelfTensorHom K L) (galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective K L)

@[simp] lemma galoisSelfTensorEquiv_tmul (a b : L) :
